heard: Hand-woven wire computers steered the first men to the moon. This machine was built by weaving copper through magnetic rings. Margaret Hamilton called this core rope memory. It held just 36 kilowords of code, all knitted by hand. The computer triggered emergency alarms during the 1969 landing. Spurious radar signals were flooding the tiny system with data, but Hamilton's software knew exactly what to ignore. It dumped low-priority tasks to keep the engine firing. This fourth astronaut saved the mission from crashing. That's how hand-woven wire computers steered the first men to the moon.
